newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end weaker, gold touch firmer.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end weaker, gold touch firmer.

text.p: New York precious metals ended weaker Wednesday in generally quiet dealings in contrast to the sharp moves earlier in the week.
"The gold market is just trading in a range," Scott Mehlman, chief dealer at Credit Lyonnais Rouse said.
"It may be a little bit short and move up first, but ultimately it's going lower," Mehlman said, expecting spot gold or bullion to test $339.00 to $340.00 an ounce.
COMEX June gold settled 30 cents firmer at $343.70 an ounce, traded $344.00 to $342.20. Bullion was quoted late afternoon by dealers at $342.70/$343.20 an ounce.

Fundamentally gold looked sound according to producer body World Gold Council whose report issued Wednesday noted that consumption in key world markets shot up 17 percent to a record 771 tonnes in the first quarter of the year.
COMEX silver ended barely changed, down 1.8 cents at $4.695 an ounce in the July contract, traded narrowly between $4.71 and $4.67.
Estimated volumes in gold and silver were 25,000 and 11,000 lots, respectively.
Platinum and palladium ended weaker following statements by Russian officials saying talks with the Japanese regarding delayed deliveries of 1997 shipments had started.
Russia will ship about the same amount of white metals this year as it did in 1996, even though five months have already passed, the officials added.
Edward Kempf of CPM Group said prices could fall back sharply once Russian metal actually moves later this month or early June.
"Then prices will inch their way back to these (current) levels after the initial shock of the fact that metal is now making its way back into the market," Kempf said.
Dealers were also going to keep a close eye on June palladium contracts as first notice day nears with high open interest in a tight physical market.
NYMEX June palladium settled $1.65 weaker at $180.10 an ounce, traded $181.50 to $177.50.
NYMEX July platinum settled $3.90 lower at $392.10 an ounce, traded $395.20 to $390.00.
